Not used: Library of Congress item 2021668747 (Agnese atlas); its roses are about 100 px across at full size, too small to crop.

Not used: Visconte Maggiolo 1541 (Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, `Maggiolo_-_Portolankarte_-_1541.png`, 1,312 × 860); its roses are about 80 px, its ships about 70 px and its tents and whale under 200 px, with rhumb lines across them.

Not used: Gabriel de Vallseca 1439 (`Gabriel_Vallseca._Museo_Marítimo,_Barcelona.1439.jpg`); 1,600 × 1,038 is the largest scan of the chart itself on Commons. The 9,144 × 6,610 `btv1b8459305b` is a reduced facsimile, not the chart.
Not yet cropped from `debry-arrival-englishmen-virginia.jpg`: the wrecked hulls, the fish weir and the grapevine. Hand colour makes it a colour-source pack, not an ink one.

Pinned, not yet cropped (charts of the New World): Agnese c. 1544; the Huntington's HM 28, catalogued as Francesco Ghisolfi, Genoa, 1550–1599, whose world sheet carries the cherub wind-heads; Desliens 1566, drawn south up; Vaz Dourado 1580; Martines 1587; Thornton 1700; Murillo Velarde 1734; and the two Pitcairn plates. The Huntington's record grants no licence; its library policy asks no permission for public-domain material, only the call number. Desliens rests on the Commons PD-Art tags; Gallica's own terms are not pinned.

Reference only, not usable: A Chart and Views of Pitcairns Island, Bayly sculp. 1773, David Rumsey Map Collection 3403.012 (4,415 × 3,499; https://davidrumsey.com/maps870029-23984.html), CC BY-NC-SA. It is the same plate as `Pitcairn_Island_accountofvoyages01hawk_0423.jpg` at 1.6 times the size.

Reference only, not usable: dealer photographs of the Pitcairn plates, Bénard 1774 at Geographicus (https://www.geographicus.com/P/AntiqueMap/pitcairn-benard-1774) and Carteret at the Antique Print & Map Room (https://antiqueprintmaproom.com/product/a-chart-and-views-of-pitcairns-island-latitude-25-philip-carteret-220922/).

Not used: Insulae Philippinae, Barent Langenes, Caert-Thresoor, Middelburg 1598, Boston Public Library G1015.L36 1598, Internet Archive `caertthresoorinh00lang` leaf 0537; a pocket-atlas page about 3,200 px wide, offered only as JPEG 2000, with nothing big enough to crop.
Library of Congress, Illustrated Guide to Sea Atlases (https://guides.loc.gov/maps-illustrated-guide/sea-atlases): a reading list for further sea atlases, not a scan.
